tool.name: CMiNet
tool.description: Construct consensus microbiome networks from abundance tables

param.name: abundance_table
param.label: Abundance table (optional)
param.help: Microbiome abundance matrix in CMiNet layout: samples in the rows, the first column holding the sample ids, and one column per taxon. Comma or tab separated, and the separator is taken from the header, so a semicolon separated file works as well. Tick 'Is the data count-based?' inside the application unless the values are relative abundances, in which case they are shifted by a small constant to keep them strictly positive. Leave this empty to upload from the browser, import from the history, or start from the example data that ships with the application.

param.name: weighted_network
param.label: Weighted network (optional)
param.help: A previously computed weighted network, used by the 'Network Visualization' and 'Final Weighted Network' tabs so that they can be opened without running the full analysis again. Comma or tab separated, the separator is taken from the header, taxa in the rows and taxa in the columns. Leave this empty to use the network the analysis itself produces.

tool.help:
`CMiNet <https://github.com/solislemuslab/CMiNet>`_ is a browser based R Shiny application for constructing consensus microbiome networks. It estimates pairwise networks with several algorithms, combines them into a single weighted consensus network and lets you explore and export the result.
.. class:: infomark
**Results are sent to your Galaxy history.** Every download has a *Send to Galaxy* button next to it. It saves the file in the *CMiNet results* collection and starts a direct history upload in the background. The collection becomes available in the history when the interactive job ends, even if direct upload is unavailable, so anything you sent during the session is kept either way.
**Input datasets.** Both inputs are optional, and the tool starts and serves the application whether or not you provide them. The abundance table you select here is staged and pre-loaded into the application. You can also import a dataset or collection element that is already in the current history straight from the application's sidebar, which is useful when the data comes out of another tool in the same analysis. Uploading a file from the browser works as usual, and the application ships with a small example dataset.
What this tool provides:
#. Network estimation with SparCC, SpiecEasi, SPRING, gCoda, CMIMN, CCLasso, Spearman, Pearson and Bicor, including the parameters each of them takes #. Weighted consensus network from the selected algorithms #. Network exploration in the 'Network Visualization' and 'Final Weighted Network' tabs #. Export of the weighted network, the edge list, and the network and binary network folders as ZIP archives
